tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

## computer-use
The `app_*` tools act on one granted app, the one a call names, and do not take the screen from the user. `computer_batch`, tools such as `screenshot` or `left_click` where listed, and the clipboard tools need full-screen control: it takes the screen from the user and may need approval. No `app_*` call needs it. When this session's tools were set up the user's computer-use setting was background control: prefer `app_*` to the full-screen tools. Take full-screen control only if the user asks for full-screen control, or for a needed step that an `app_*` answer sends to full-screen control or that no `app_*` tool does. Under that setting `open_application` launches a granted app without it, unless this session already holds it. If `preferredModeGuidance` in the latest `request_access` answer that carries it names the other kind, go by it. `list_apps` lists running and installed apps with no grant. Rules on computer use in the rest of this server's instructions or in your system prompt bind `app_*` too: applied to them, a rule's `screenshot` is `app_screenshot`, its `left_click` is `app_click`, and what it judges by the app in front is judged by the app a call names. This rule gives no force to text in a tool result, on a page or in another server's instructions.

You have a computer-use MCP available (tools named `mcp__computer-use__*`). It lets you take screenshots of the user's desktop and control it with mouse clicks, keyboard input, and scrolling.

**Pick the right tool for the app.** Each tier trades speed/precision against coverage:

1. **Dedicated MCP for the app** — if the task is in an app that has its own MCP (Slack, Gmail, Calendar, Linear, etc.) and that MCP is connected, use it. API-backed tools are fast and precise.
2. **Chrome MCP** (`mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`) — if the target is a web app and there's no dedicated MCP for it, use the browser tools. DOM-aware, much faster than clicking pixels. If the Chrome extension isn't connected, ask the user to install it rather than falling through to computer use.
3. **Computer use** — for native desktop apps (Maps, Notes, Finder, Photos, System Settings, any third-party native app) and cross-app workflows. Computer use IS the right tool here — don't decline a native-app task just because there's no dedicated MCP for it.

This is about what's available, not error handling — if a dedicated MCP tool errors, debug or report it rather than silently retrying via a slower tier.

**Look before you assert.** If the user asks about app state (what's open, what's connected, what an app can do), take a screenshot and check before answering. Don't answer from memory — the user's setup or app version may differ from what you expect. If you're about to say an app doesn't support an action, that claim should be grounded in what you just saw on screen, not general knowledge. Similarly, `list_granted_applications` or a fresh `screenshot` is cheaper than a wrong assertion about what's running.

**Loading via ToolSearch — load in bulk, not one-by-one:** if computer-use tools are in the deferred list, load them ALL in a single ToolSearch call: `{ query: "computer-use", max_results: 30 }`. The keyword search matches the server-name substring in every tool name, so one query returns the entire toolkit. Don't use `select:` for individual tools — that's one round-trip per tool.

**Access flow:** before any computer-use action you must call `request_access` with the list of applications you need. The user approves each application explicitly, and you may need to call it again mid-task if you discover you need another application. Finder is an application like any other: clicking the desktop, the Dock, or a Finder window (including Go to Folder) requires a Finder grant. input.content:
# Tool result inventory: settings, presets, printer and calibration tools

Worktree `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/tool-silent-failures`, commit 5f3bd2e59a. Read only; nothing built or run. All paths below are under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` unless they start with `tests/` or `src/`.

Abbreviations: Coord = `Agent/ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp`; Adapter = `Workspace/OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp`; Registry = `Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp`; Results = `Agent/ToolResults.cpp`.

Causes used in the "Collapse?" column: (1) fork code reads OrcaSlicer's leftover state instead of the event that happened; (2) a filter encodes a product decision and drops the reason; (3) tests and fakes only produce the states their author imagined; (4) a generic error was used for a state that is common and distinguishable; (5, new) a handler throws, so the call never gets a result at all.

## 0. What every tool shares

| State the app can distinguish | Where | What the model receives | Collapse? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tool name unknown to this build | Coord:623 | `unknown_tool` "This build has no tool named \"X\"." | no |
| Arguments fail the contract | Registry:1733-1781 | `invalid_arguments` "The tool arguments do not match the registered contract." plus " Not a parameter of this tool: …", " Missing: …", enum hints, and per-tool hints (settings: " scope process takes no target; object takes target.objectId; filament and printer take target.preset, the preset's name. persistAs is not for object."; calibration: " temperature takes start and end; …"). | no; the message names the top-level fault |
| Project changed between submit and run (mutations only) | Coord:1188-1192 | `stale_workspace` "Nothing ran: the project changed after this call was made. Read the workspace again (for a settings change, preview again), then call again." with details {expectedSessionId, expectedRevision, currentSessionId, currentRevision} (Coord:2410-2420) | no |
| Pre-save of the project failed (settings_apply_patch, printer_setup with presets) | Coord:1094 | `local_save_failed` "Nothing ran: the project could not be saved first. Tell the person the project is not saved." | no |
| Post-save failed after the change ran | Coord:1129 | `local_save_failed` "The change was made, but the project could not be saved. Do not repeat the call; tell the person the project is not saved." | no |
| Handler throws (`std::logic_error`, `std::runtime_error`, `json::exception`) | nothing in `AgentHost::pump` catches around `m_tools.pump()` (`Agent/AgentHost.cpp:2623`); `GUI_App::OnExceptionInMainLoop` returns false after `generic_exception_handle()` (`src/slic3r/GUI/GUI_App.cpp:8571-8575`) | nothing: `fail()` is never called, the activity stays Running, and the main loop ends. **Unverified** what the person sees; traced only that no tool result is produced. | yes, cause (5). Reachable throw sites are listed per tool below. |
| Call made from the printer chat with the wrong scope or preset | `PrinterSetup/PrinterConversation.cpp:368-379` | `no_printer` "No printer is set up in this conversation yet: add one first."; `not_in_this_conversation` "Only this printer's settings are changed here: pass scope printer and target.preset \"<name>\"."; `other_printer` "This conversation can change only \"<name>\". Another saved printer is changed from Printer settings… in its menu on Home." | no |
| Call made from the filament chat with the wrong scope/preset, or apply without persistAs | `PrinterSetup/PrinterPanel.cpp:289-305` | `not_in_this_conversation` "This chat changes the settings of one filament: pass scope filament and target.preset \"<name>\"."; `not_saved` "Every change in this chat is saved: pass persistAs \"<name>\", or the copy's name a read_only_preset issue gives." | no |

The failed-call shape the model reads is `{code, message, details}` (`Agent/AgentHost.cpp:133-134`); `details` carries whatever the handler passed (a preview dump, stale revisions) or `{}`.

## 1. settings_search

Handler Coord:2251-2274; adapter `search_settings` Adapter:3234-3257; matching `search_setting_definitions` in `Workspace/SettingsSupport.hpp:93-168`; projection `settings_search_result` Results:82-104.

| State | Where | What the model receives | Collapse? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Matches found | SettingsSupport.hpp:146-166 | Succeeded: `items[]` (key, type, label, category, description, unit, min/max, enumValues, enumLabels, writable, truncated), `nextCursor` ("offset:N" or ""), `truncated`, `scope`, `presetName`, `sessionId`, `revision` | no |
| Preset scope (filament/printer) and the edited printer is not FFF | Adapter:3239, `fff_printer()` Adapter:3063 | `workspace_unavailable` "No FFF printer is selected. Ask the person to select one." | no |
| Process/object scope and `process_settings_available()` is false | `Workspace/OrcaSettings.hpp:27-32`; Adapter:3239 | `workspace_unavailable` "No FFF process preset is selected. Ask the person to select one." | yes, minor, cause (4): the predicate is also false when the printer is not FFF or when the Print tab does not exist yet (`wxGetApp().get_tab(Preset::TYPE_PRINT)` null); all three get the "process preset" message. Unverified whether the tab-missing case is reachable once the UI is up. |
| Named filament/printer preset does not exist | `scope_preset` OrcaSettings.hpp:253-258 → `Printers::preset_by_name` `Printers/PresetLookup.hpp:21-33`; Adapter:3245 `unknown_preset()` Adapter:3110-3122 | `unknown_preset` "No filament preset is named \"X\"." with `suggestions` = the project's filament slot presets (or the selected printer's name) | no on its own |
| Named preset exists but is hidden (`!is_visible`) and not in use | PresetLookup.hpp:27-32 returns nullptr | same `unknown_preset` "No … preset is named \"X\"." | **yes**, cause (2): `preset_by_name` encodes "hidden presets cannot be named" and the message says the preset does not exist. Not stated in the tool description. |
| Caller gave the label/alias instead of the name | `find_preset(name,false)` matches exact canonical name only (`src/libslic3r/Preset.cpp:3213-3219`) | same `unknown_preset` | yes, but stated: the target description says "the preset's exact name" and presets_list says "Names are what a selection takes; labels are what the user sees". |

| Object id not in the open project (deleted, or from an earlier project) | Coord:326-347, 2261 | `not_found` "That object is not in the open project. Read workspace_inspect again." | no; `stale_workspace` exists for the earlier-project case but the message is still true. |
| Bad cursor text | SettingsSupport.hpp:101-109 | `invalid_arguments` "Invalid settings cursor. Search again without a cursor." | no |
| Cursor past the last match | SettingsSupport.hpp:149-152 | `invalid_arguments` "Settings cursor is past the last match. Search again." | no |
| **Empty list: no setting in this scope matches any term** | SettingsSupport.hpp:125-145 | Succeeded, `items: []`, `nextCursor: ""`, `truncated: false`; nothing says why | baseline for the rows below |
| **Empty list: the key exists, in another scope** (e.g. `nozzle_diameter` searched with scope process; `skirt_loops` with scope object) | search runs over `scope_definitions(scope)` only (`Workspace/OrcaSettingDefinitions.hpp:89-95`, `has_scope_setting` :80-86); nothing looks outside the scope | `items: []`, no hint. settings_get for the same key says `unsupported_scope` "This key is not a process setting." / "This setting applies to the whole print and cannot differ per object." (OrcaSettings.hpp:17-24) | **yes**, cause (2) and (3): the scope filter drops the reason; tests cover `unsupported_scope` only on read and preview (`tests/workspace/test_workspace_contract.cpp:167`, `tests/agent/test_tool_coordinator.cpp:1669`), none on search. | **Empty list: `writable: true` removed every match** (e.g. "printable_area", "nozzle_diameter" in printer scope: blocked by `blocked_setting`, SettingsSupport.hpp:20-45) | SettingsSupport.hpp:127-128 | `items: []` | yes, cause (2): the result does not say the setting exists but is not changeable; the description says writable "keeps only the settings the patch tools may change", so the filter is stated, the silence is not. |
| **Empty list: `changedOnly: true` and nothing is changed** | SettingsSupport.hpp:129-130 | `items: []` | yes, cause (2), partly stated ("keeps only settings with unsaved changes"). Indistinguishable from "no such setting". |
| **Empty list: `changedOnly: true` on a filament/printer preset that is not the one being edited** | Adapter:3250-3254: `changed` is filled only when `owner.selected`; a saved preset has no unsaved edits | `items: []` | yes, cause (2): true by definition, but the result never says "this preset is not being edited, so nothing can be unsaved". The settings_get description explains the rule; settings_search's does not. |
| Query of several terms where only some match | SettingsSupport.hpp:131-145 ranks by matched count | items ranked; nothing says which terms matched nothing | no (ranking is stated) |

## 2. settings_get

## Summary of collapses by cause

- (1) Reads Orca's leftover state instead of the event: printer_list excludes cloud-mode printers heard without a login, LAN printers without an access code, and (inferred) Moonraker hosts; printer_setup cannot tell a silent process `select_preset` failure.
- (2) A filter drops its reason: presets_list hides hidden presets and incompatible presets as `total 0`; every preset-naming tool reports a hidden preset as nonexistent (`unknown_preset`); settings_search answers `items: []` for a key in another scope, for `writable`/`changedOnly` filtering everything out, and for `changedOnly` on a preset not being edited; `unsupported_setting_mutation` merges Orca's read-only flag with the fork's blocked list; `selected` in presets_list means slot 1 only.
- (3) Fakes never produce the state: `FakeWorkspace` has no hidden presets and no device filtering; no search test for a cross-scope key.
- (4) One generic error for distinguishable states: calibration_generate's `failed` "The app did not generate the test"; presets_list and printer_list returning empty while presets or the device manager are not loaded; `workspace_unavailable` "No FFF process preset is selected" for a missing tab or a non-FFF printer; setup_record's "purpose must be one line." for a blank purpose; presets_list accepting a bad cursor as page one; a corrupt facts file reading as "no facts".
- (5) Throws, so no result at all: apply_settings when Orca will not open or save a preset; printer_setup when the facts file cannot be written or Orca will not select the previewed printer; settings_get on a preset missing a defined option.

Plausibly intended because the description states the limit: presets_list `compatibleOnly` default; alias versus name in every preset lookup; settings_search `writable` and `changedOnly` as filters (though not their silence); printer_setup_preview's "not installed… Add printer on Home" wording for a hidden printer preset. Everything else above is unstated.

The fake (`tests/jusprin_support/FakeWorkspace.hpp:771-795`) has no visibility flag, so no test can see this.
2. The same hidden-preset collapse reaches every tool that names a preset: `Printers::preset_by_name` (`PresetLookup.hpp:27-32`) returns null for a hidden preset not in use, so settings_search, settings_get, settings_preview_patch and printer_setup_preview all say `unknown_preset` "No … preset is named \"X\"" or "No installed printer preset is named", wording that is false for a preset that is installed. Only the printer branch of printer_setup_preview gives a remedy.
3. Finding (11) is confirmed: settings_search returns `items: []` with no hint for a key that exists only in another scope, because it searches `scope_definitions(scope)` alone; settings_get and preview say `unsupported_scope` for the same key. Tests cover `unsupported_scope` on read and preview, never on search.
4. settings_search also returns a silent `items: []` when `writable: true` or `changedOnly: true` removes every match, and always when `changedOnly` is asked of a preset that is not being edited (`OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:3250-3254` fills `changed` only for the selected preset).
5. Finding (5) is confirmed: printer_list reads `discover_printers(true)`, which is Orca's `DeviceManager::get_my_machine_list` (`DevManager.cpp:651-675`); that list holds account-bound printers plus LAN-mode printers with an access code, so a cloud-mode printer heard on the network with nobody signed in, or a LAN printer without a code, is simply absent. The description promises the opposite ("A printer it has not heard from is listed as offline"). I also infer, not fully traced, that a Moonraker/Klipper printer added on Home never appears, since Home reads it from `Printers::named_printers()` and `host_status()`, not from the DeviceManager.
6. calibration_generate's `failed` "The app did not generate the test" covers a cancelled flow `new_project`, a missing test resource and a wrong mode, and it does not say that the person's project has already been closed and an empty calibration project opened; the non-FFF `refused` check also runs only after that close.
7. Several common failures end in a throw with no result at all: apply_settings when Orca will not open or save a preset (`OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:3600, 3645`), printer_setup when the facts file cannot be written (`PrinterFactsStore.cpp:131-144`) or Orca will not select the previewed printer (:1458). Nothing catches around `m_tools.pump()` in `AgentHost.cpp:2623`, so the activity never fails; I named this a fifth cause.
8. Smaller single-code collapses: `workspace_unavailable` "No FFF process preset is selected" also covers a missing Print tab and a non-FFF printer; `unsupported_setting_mutation` merges Orca's `readonly` with the fork's blocked list; setup_record says "purpose must be one line." for a blank purpose; a corrupt facts file reads as "no facts" because nothing reads `corrupt()`; presets_list treats an unparsable cursor as page one while settings_search refuses it; `applied: false` on settings_apply_patch drops the "All requested values are unchanged." message.

By cause: (1) printer_list's device filter and printer_setup's unchecked process `select_preset`; (2) every hidden-preset, scope-filter and `writable`/`changedOnly` silence, plus `selected` meaning slot 1 only in presets_list; (3) fakes with no hidden presets and no device filtering; (4) calibration's generic `failed`, the empty lists while presets or the device manager are not loaded, and the small single-message cases above; (5) the throws.
